title: Price Action Basics
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/0/body: **Price action** means making decisions by reading **price itself**: candles, highs and lows, and key levels. Indicators are built from that same price, so price action means going straight to the **original source**.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/0/tip: Price action keeps your chart clean, but it takes a lot of practice and patience.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/1/body: In an **uptrend**, price makes **higher highs (HH)** and **higher lows (HL)**. In a **downtrend**, it makes **lower highs (LH)** and **lower lows (LL)**. Reading this structure is step one of price action.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/2/promp: What's the structure of this chart?
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/2/expla: Each high is below the one before, and each low is below the last low. That's a bearish structure of LH and LL.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/3/promp: Tap the candle that shows the strongest selling pressure.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/3/expla: The biggest red body, with almost no wicks. Sellers were in full control from the open to the close.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/4/title: What do bodies and wicks say?
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/4/body: A **big body** means one side was firmly in control. A **long wick** means price tested an area and got **rejected**. A **small body** means indecision, a balance between buyers and sellers.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/5/state: A long lower wick shows that price was rejected in that area.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/5/expla: Sellers pushed price down, but buyers brought it back by the close. The long wick is the footprint of that rejection.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/6/promp: After a strong rally, candles get smaller and upper wicks get longer. What's the most sensible read?
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/6/optio: Price will definitely reverse right now
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/6/expla: Small bodies and upper wicks mean buyers can't push price up easily anymore. It's a warning, not a guaranteed reversal.
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/7/pairs: A peak above the previous peak
A dip above the previous dip
A peak below the previous peak
A dip below the previous dip
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/8/promp: The trend is up, and after a pullback price made a higher low. The last candle has a long lower wick. Which way is more likely?
lessons/price-action-u1-l1/steps/8/expla: The HH and HL structure is intact, and the last candle shows price rejected from a higher low. Continuation up is more likely. Stop loss below that HL.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/0/body: **Key levels** are places where price has **reacted** several times before: major highs and lows, range edges, and levels that broke. Price action traders look for their setups **right at these levels**.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/1/body: Price rarely turns at one exact number; **wicks** often poke a little past the level. That's why it's better to see a level as a **narrow zone**, not a line one pip thick.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/1/tip: Draw the level where most touches are, not on one unusual wick.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/2/expla: Price reached this level several times and dropped back. Sellers are active there, so it's resistance.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/3/promp: The yellow line is key resistance. Tap the candle that tested it with its wick but didn't close above it.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/3/expla: This candle's upper wick poked past 62,000, but the body closed well below. Sellers rejected price at resistance.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/4/promp: Price hit the same high several times and got pushed back. Drag the resistance line onto that zone.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/4/expla: Price reached 63,950 to 64,020 three times and got pushed back, so resistance is around 64,000, which is also a round number. Remember: a level is a zone, not an exact line.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/5/state: The more often a level gets tested, the stronger it always becomes.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/5/expla: More touches show a level matters, but each test uses up some of the orders sitting there. Many traders believe a level that's been hit again and again is more likely to break.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/6/title: Round numbers and previous highs and lows
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/6/body: **Round numbers** (like 1.1000 or $60,000) and **the previous day's or week's high and low** attract lots of orders and often become key levels. When a structural level lines up with a round number, it matters even more.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/7/promp: Which level is probably more important?
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/7/optio: A high that rejected price three times, sitting at 1.1000
The price of a random candle mid-range
A level price has never reacted to
The open of the current candle
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/7/expla: Several past reactions plus a round number means lots of orders have piled up there. The other options have no history of reactions.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/8/sente: It's better to see levels as a ___, not an exact line, because ___ often poke a little past them.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/8/expla: Price pokes past a level with its wicks and comes back. If you see the level as a zone, those swings won't fool you.
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/9/promp: Price reached the support zone for the second time, and the last candle closed bullish with a lower wick. What's your call?
lessons/price-action-u1-l2/steps/9/expla: This zone already turned price once, and now buyers rejected price from it again. A move up is more likely. Stop loss just below the zone.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/0/body: A **pin bar** is a candle with a **long wick** (about two thirds of the candle or more) and a **small body** at the other end. The wick shows price tested an area and got **sharply rejected**.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/1/body: A pin bar in the middle of nowhere isn't worth much. It means something when it forms at a **key level**, ideally **with the trend**, like a bullish pin bar on support.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/2/promp: What's the last candle at resistance?
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/2/expla: A long upper wick and a small body at the bottom, right at resistance: price got rejected above the level. This is a bearish pin bar.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/3/promp: Tap the candle that formed a bullish pin bar on support.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/3/expla: This candle has a very long lower wick below support and a small body near its high. A classic bullish pin bar, and price rose after it.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/4/state: A bullish pin bar has its long wick at the bottom and its small body near the high.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/4/expla: Sellers pushed price down but got rejected, and price closed near the high. A long upper wick belongs to a bearish pin bar.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/5/title: Pin bar entry and stop loss
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/5/body: A common approach: enter on a **break of the pin bar's high** (for a bullish pin) with a **stop loss just below the wick's tip**. Some traders use a limit order around the **50% level of the pin bar** instead, for a tighter stop.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/6/promp: Bullish pin bar on BTC: entry above the pin's high, stop loss below the wick's tip. Where's take profit at 1:2?
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/7/promp: After a drop, a bullish pin bar formed and your entry is just above its high. Where do you put your stop loss?
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/7/expla: A pin bar's stop loss goes just below the tip of its long wick, so below 1.2610 (say 1.2605). That wick is where sellers got rejected; if price drops past it again, the setup is invalid.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/8/promp: In a downtrend, price rallied back to resistance at 1.1000 and formed a bearish pin bar. What's your call?
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/8/expla: A bearish pin bar at resistance, with the downtrend, on a round number. Continuation down is more likely. Stop loss just above the wick's tip.
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/9/promp: A bullish pin bar formed in the middle of a strong downtrend, far from any level. What do you do?
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/9/optio: Skip it: no level and no trend behind it
Buy right away with a big position
Sell, because it's a bullish pin bar
Skip the stop loss, since pin bars are strong
lessons/price-action-u1-l3/steps/9/expla: A pin bar with no key level and against the trend has low odds of working. Price action means waiting for setups that form in the right place.
